overview.text: Today's developments showcase significant advances across model capabilities, theoretical physics applications, and safety research. A frontier model has demonstrated the ability to directly edit the weights of a much smaller model, bypassing traditional static deployment limitations. In scientific applications, Claude Fable 5.2 successfully solved two open problems in black hole physics, marking a notable milestone for theoretical research. Additionally, new approaches in spatial intelligence via interactive workflows and methods like AltRA-Test are helping evaluate LLM judges more reliably without shared annotators. In safety and infrastructure, OpenAI detailed its layered defenses against adversarial distillation to protect against capability extraction, while new work explores formal verification to combat software slop. Meanwhile, open-source releases continue to drive high activity, and discussions on alignment highlight ongoing urgency around short-term takeover risks.

entries.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
entries.summary: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one.
entries.why: Enables models to edit smaller model weights directly, moving beyond static post-training deployment paradigms.

entries.title: Claude Fable 5.2 solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
entries.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 has solved two open problems in theoretical physics. Both concern black holes and the search for a theory of quantum gravity.
entries.why: Demonstrates successful resolution of open theoretical physics problems regarding black holes and quantum gravity.

entries.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
entries.summary: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same?
entries.why: Grounds multimodal large language models in interactive 3D spatial actions using CAPTCHAs.

entries.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
entries.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified.
entries.why: Introduces an alternative annotator test for statistically justifying LLM judges without shared annotators.

entries.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
entries.summary: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover.
entries.why: Provides online mistake detection for procedural video assistants to intervene before recovery becomes impossible.

entries.title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
entries.summary: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews.
entries.why: Measures claim-level critique overlap in peer review to understand peer review homogenization.

entries.title: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
entries.summary: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale.
entries.why: Combines camera input and IMU data for universal online metric localization and dense mapping.

entries.title: DavidAU/Qwen3.8-27B-TURBO-Fable-Cold-Fusion-735-882-Heretic-Uncensored-NEO-CODER-MAX-MTP-GGUF
entries.why: Provides a heavily customized community model release with extensive naming and architecture tags.

entries.title: unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF
entries.why: Delivers widely downloaded GGUF weights for the Qwen3.8-27B architecture.

entries.title: mankidev/antialgorithm
entries.summary: Agent skill that steers the model away from its first, most average pick in creative work: names, ideas, logo, posters, UI. · Python
entries.why: Offers an agent skill designed to steer generative models away from average creative choices.

entries.title: How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini
entries.why: Highlights the evolution of Google Duplex integration within Gemini for calling businesses.

entries.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
entries.summary: OpenAI’s layered approach to adversarial distillation combines model training, safeguards, detection, and enforcement to protect against capability extraction.
entries.why: Outlines layered safeguards and detection mechanisms to protect against capability extraction via adversarial distillation.

entries.title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
entries.summary: Proving software correct with math has traditionally required specialist work. Now AI and Lean are helping automate the process.
entries.why: Explores how AI and Lean are automating formal verification to fight software slop.

entries.title: On Dwarkesh Patel’s November 2026 Podcast With Paul Christiano
entries.summary: Paul Christiano has a message for us: There is meaningful risk of AI taking over within even the next 6-12 months.
entries.why: Examines discussions on near-term AI takeover risks within the coming months.

entries.title: Jensen Huang Really Liked Selling China Advanced AI Chips
entries.summary: This scandal is a really big deal.
entries.why: Discusses controversy and business practices surrounding advanced AI chip sales to China.
